x: They had the first two home in Dee and Brickwood; and although our boys finished 4, 5, 6, 7, it was not good enough! Thus at the end of the evening the points up to date were: Belgrave H., 29; Mitcham A.C., 27; Epsom H., 12; Croydon H., 12.
Mitcham were also now in front of Birchfield in the team race and the four Welsh members of their scoring six all ran well to assist Thorogood and Brickwood in gaining team honours.

Brickwood led in the next lap with Hoath still second, Herbert was 3rd and Carter had dropped back to 4th. The finish saw Herbert in front clocking 42.42; Hoath 2nd, 42.49; Carter 4th, 43.3; Tobin 15th, 44.44; Bryan 17th, 44.49; Cohen 18th, 45.4; Peck 21st, 45.15; Shields 25th, 45.34; Morrell 40th,…
Truly a wonderful finish and reminiscent of that of years ago when Brickwood of Mitcham beat our own Arthur Allum in the finishing straight.
The course was about 8 miles and the first man home was Archie Bedford, who beat a couple of Walton boys, with Len Adams and Denis Brickwood next home for us.

At 4½ miles Denis Brickwood was nicely placed 29th and running strongly but steadily. Arthur Whitehead, Jock McDonald and Bill Wortley were close behind, while the rest of our lads were among the 100s.

Charlie Walker again refused to cane himself over the last mile and was content with 4th. Following him were Tooby, Bedford, Burr, Trower, Brickwood, L. Bishop and Newell making one of his too infrequent appearances.
Cliff Roffey came through for second, Short 3rd., Walker 5th and then the pack Bagnall, Gebbett, Burr, Brickwood and Trower 7th to 11th to make sure of the team race.
1, Flanagan, 51.25; 6, Cousens, 55.42; 7, Bishop.A, 56.31; 8, Boreham.S, 56.50; 9, Szucik, 57.05; 10, Brickwood, 57.35; 11, Penstone, 57.35; 17, Jones, 62.40; 18, Matthews - off course.
Earlier in the year we had finished 2nd in the English Cross Country Championships and then 2nd in the Brighton Relay - due very much to Mitcham’s Brickwood beating us to the line.
